findings.title: A second apostrophe closes the first one's quote, so a non-orbit line can still hide an orbit line

walk_entry.title: An unclosed quote on a non-orbit shell line hides every later orbit line in the fence

findings.recommendation: Walk 1's fix covers a quote still open at the fence's end, but not one that a LATER non-orbit line closes. The orbit line between them is joined into that quoted string, with no snippet and no failure, and the row's new clause "so a line of another tool cannot hide the `orbit` lines after it" is false for it. The shell agrees the line is data (sh -n accepts it), so this is the extractor matching shell semantics; the hole is that a documented command can sit inside another command's quote unseen. Either (A) fail a join that began on a non-tool line when any joined line's first token is the tool, naming that line, or (B) narrow the clause to a quote still open at the fence's end and name the closed-later case in the places limit.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: In extractFenceLines, when a join began on a line whose first token is not the tool, fail extraction for each joined line whose first token is the tool, naming its own line. Add the two-apostrophe injection.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Narrow the quoted-argument row's last clause to a quote still open at the fence's end, and add to the places limit's residual kind: an orbit line inside a quote another line opens and a later line closes.

findings.title: A trailing backslash on a command that takes a positional passes silently, not as a false failure

walk_entry.title: The places limit omits three forms the extractor and guard both miss

findings.recommendation: Walk 1's new residual text says a continuation's `\` reaches the parser as an argument, "a false failure". That holds for a command with no positional (`orbit list \` fails as too many arguments), but `orbit validate \` parses with `\` as its item, and the continued `--frobnicate` on the next line is never checked: not extracted, and the guard skips shell-fence lines. Say both outcomes: a false failure, or a silent pass of the continued flags.

commentary: Graded the two walk logs over each entry's sweep scope, probing each repaired rule with constructed fences rather than reading. The repaired tokenizer, the exit-code rule, the requiredOption row, the NO_COLOR assertion, the generated-content surfaces and the touchpoints example all hold; the residual diff from the base file's commit lists only files inside the entries' edit records. Both regressions are the same shape: walk 1 repaired the case the finding constructed and then wrote a sentence wider than the repair. The open-quote fix fails a quote nobody closes, but the new clause claims no other tool's line can hide an orbit line, and a second apostrophe defeats it; the continuation text calls the residual loud where a positional-taking command makes it silent. Neither is on today's surface: the sweep still reads 130 parsed, 35 bare, 0 failures, 0 guard hits. Pass 0 (verify-change) and Pass 6 (audit-drift) are whole-change and whole-project and were not run in this verification pass; Passes 4 and 5 have no lens files.
